confirmed.title: Worker crash leaves the runtime FSM stuck in RUNNING with no terminal/FAILED status and no MATCH_ENDED

confirmed.title: Sudden-death convergence is side-biased: the later mech_id always wins with full HP
confirmed.evidence: _apply_sudden_death iterates `for mech in sorted(self.fold.state.living_mechs(), key=lambda item: item.mech_id)` and breaks the loop on the FIRST kill (`if self.fold.state.status is not SOMatchStatus.RUNNING: break`, lines 868-869; MECH_DESTROYED at 887-895). So on the killing tick the alphabetically-first mech takes the escalating pressure `damage = base * (tick-start+1)`, dies, victory is declared, and the loop breaks BEFORE the opponent receives that tick's identical lethal pressure. I ran three symmetric no-cap matches (identical proof_red/blue_defensive_passive loadouts) at seeds 17/99/1234: every run gave winner=player.b, destroyed=[mech.a.01], final_hp={mech.a.01:0, mech.b.01:12}. The seeded MatchRng never touches this path.

This breaks the side-swap symmetry the runner's own initiative comment (lines 431-438) says the learning loop relies on, poisoning promotion/fitness signals and producing an illegible, unshareable terminal.

Order tie resolution through initiative + MatchRng like weapon exchanges, not raw mech_id sort.

confirmed.title: Two consecutive heat-locked rounds crash the match: previous_plan is rebuilt from free-registers-only plan_committed
confirmed.evidence: Both cadences rebuild seat memory from plan_committed only: paced `self._card_previous_plans = {plan.seat: plan for plan in sequence.plan_committed}` (runner.py:751) and atomic (runner.py:590). plan_committed contains ONLY the free (unlocked) registers (validate_plan in registers.py:82-96 requires the plan to program exactly the free registers). lock_depth is derived each round from live heat: `lock_depth = int(mech.boiler.status_redline) + int(mech.overloaded)` (runner.py:617). registers._resolve_one, for a locked index, does `previous_card_id = context.card_at(context.previous_plan, index)` and `if previous_card_id is None: raise RegisterPlanError(...has no prior card to repeat)` (registers.py:144-149). produce() → CardRoundRuntime.sequence() → reducer.resolve_round is called with no try/except in _run_paced_card_round (runner.py:648, 503).

Round N is redlined → index 4 locked, resolves HEAT_LOCKED from round N-1, and round N's plan_committed OMITS index 4. confirmed.title: Promotion is an in-memory flag / YAML file, never an event
confirmed.evidence: The live promotion is `self.current_policy = next_policy` (live.py:162) — a mutation of a dataclass field guarded by an RLock. The resulting `ModelSOLiveLearningOutcome` (promoted/rejected/stale) is returned in-memory and discarded by the caller (after_match.py:62 ignores the return value); it is never published to the bus or written to the ledger. The offline path is no better: cli/learn.py:116 persists a promotion only as a YAML lineage record via `artifacts.write_lineage` (filesystem_artifacts.py:143), not as a ledger event. Confirmed there is NO promotion/policy/learning member in `SOEventType` (events/envelope.py enum ends at CARDS_DISCARDED) and no code writes a policy event (`grep POLICY|policy_after|current_policy` outside live.py/contract returns nothing).
confirmed.failure_mode: `current_policy` is lost on process restart and is not reconstructable from the event stream, violating R5 (state must be derivable purely from events). Which policy is 'current' also depends on the wall-clock ORDERING of concurrent match completions (the stale-vs-promote branch at live.py:143), an ordering recorded in no event — so the live-learning state is both non-durable and non-deterministic. This is exactly the 'promotion as an in-memory flag' the finish line forbids.
confirmed.recommendation: Add a closed `POLICY_PROMOTED`/`POLICY_FIELDED` event type carrying policy_id, spec_hash, source_lineage_digest, generation, and parent spec_hash; emit it through the event factory into the ledger on every promotion; reconstruct `current_policy` by folding that event stream rather than holding a mutable field. Record it in ledger evidence so replay reproduces the promotion.
confirmed.verify_reason: All factual claims verify: live.py:162 mutates current_policy in memory under an RLock, after_match.py:62 discards the returned outcome, SOEventType (events/envelope.py) ends at CARDS_DISCARDED with no policy/promotion event, cli/learn.py:116 persists via write_lineage -> YAML (filesystem_artifacts.py:143), and the stale-vs-promote branch at live.py:143 makes 'current' depend on completion order; but the in-memory path is dead code (never runs) and the working offline path's durable content-addressed YAML lineage records are a legitimate evidence surface, so blocker overstates it — high.

confirmed.title: Promotion-port seam omits match admission; coordinator can never be driven through it
confirmed.evidence: `AfterMatchLearningHandler` consumes `LiveLearningPromotionPort` (live.py:37), whose ONLY method is `handle_after_match(evidence)`. But the concrete `LiveLearningCoordinator.handle_after_match` first looks up `snapshot = self._active.get(evidence.match_id)` and, if absent, raises `match ... must be admitted before terminal evidence` (live.py:104-109). The admission call `begin_match` is NOT part of the port the handler holds, and nothing in the match runtime calls it. So if the real coordinator were passed as the promotion port, EVERY terminal `MATCH_SCORED` would raise inside the bus callback (after_match.py:62). The handler also discards the returned outcome, so even a successful promotion result is unobservable.
confirmed.failure_mode: The two halves of the live-learning seam (begin_match admission, handle_after_match terminal) are never connected to a real match lifecycle. Wiring the coordinator as-is would crash match scoring on the first completed match, or (if the exception is swallowed by the bus) silently drop every promotion. This is a field-by-field boundary mismatch: the admitting side and the terminal side share no wired call path.
confirmed.recommendation: Extend the port (or the composition) so the match runtime calls `begin_match(match_id)` at admission and the same coordinator instance receives `handle_after_match` at terminal; propagate/emit the returned `ModelSOLiveLearningOutcome` instead of discarding it. Add a cross-boundary regression test that admits then completes a real match.

confirmed.title: Transport terminal guard hard-throws on the draw scoring path (match_scored emitted after match_ended), breaking replay and the end-of-match scorecard

confirmed.title: Event boundary accepts arbitrary payloads — no event_type↔payload validation, closedness is convention-only
confirmed.evidence: ModelSOEventEnvelope declares `payload: FrozenJSONMapping` (envelope.py:97). The only model_validator (`_envelope_entity_matches_match_id`, l.103) never consults `event_type` or the `CURRENT_CONSUMED_PAYLOAD_MODELS` registry, and neither does `make_event`/`EventFactory.make`. Runtime-proven: `EventFactory.make(event_type=MATCH_TICK, payload={'kind':...,'tick':3,'garbage_field':999})` builds and freezes a valid envelope with `garbage_field` intact, even though `ModelSOEmptyPayload.model_validate(...)` REJECTS that same payload with `extra_forbidden`. The project's own tests/events/test_factory.py:45 builds a MATCH_TICK event whose payload `{'kind':...,'tick':3}` and l.67 a HAND_DEALT event whose payload `{'seat':'a'}` BOTH fail their canonical authorities (extra_forbidden / missing) yet are accepted at the boundary.
confirmed.failure_mode: A producer (or a drifted/buggy handler) emits `event_type=WEAPON_FIRED` with a garbage or misshapen payload. The envelope accepts it, the ledger persists it verbatim, replay reloads it, and the failure only surfaces later at an arbitrary consumer's `model_validate` (or never, for consumers that read raw). The R3 mandate 'unknown fields rejected at the boundary; event models are extra=forbid' is not met for payload content — the boundary is closed for envelope metadata but open for the actual game data.
confirmed.recommendation: Add an `@model_validator(mode='after')` on ModelSOEventEnvelope that resolves `CURRENT_CONSUMED_PAYLOAD_MODELS[event_type]` and calls `.model_validate(self.payload)` (fail-closed for event types with a registered authority; explicit allow-list for the few emitted-but-open types). This makes the closed-payload contract enforced at construction/deserialization rather than deferred to each consumer.

confirmed.title: Split-deck matches emit no card-runtime provenance; card/deck content hash is absent from the event stream

The `provenance` property returns None whenever `selected_deck_id is None` (card_runtime.py:120-121), which is exactly the split-deck path (the overlay uses `deck_policy`, not `deck_id`, so `selected_deck_id` stays None). Replay's check then compares None==None vacuously (replay/engine.py:284, replay/card_round.py:465).

confirmed.title: Bus re-raises every subscriber exception as one ExceptionGroup — no critical/best-effort tiering, no atomicity between ledger and fold
confirmed.evidence: InProcessEventBus.publish (in_process.py:69-79) collects ALL subscriber exceptions and raises `ExceptionGroup("subscriber errors", errors)` after firing every subscriber, treating authoritative subscribers (ledger.append @ composition.py:1836, fold.handle @ runner.py:275) identically to best-effort ones (the WebSocket broadcaster `_on_event` @ cli/serve.py:299, the CLI renderer @ projections/cli/renderer.py:97). cli/serve.py:327-329 `_on_event` raises RuntimeError if the loop is not started and calls `self.serialize(event)` (model_dump_json) inline before the threadsafe handoff.
confirmed.failure_mode: Because publish() is called from the match tick loop (runner.py:336..), any raised ExceptionGroup propagates and aborts the authoritative match. A best-effort transport/UI subscriber failure (WS serialize error, renderer bug, or the loop-not-started RuntimeError) therefore kills the live sim — directly undermining a clean-browser real-provider demo. Worse, there is no atomicity: if the ledger already appended but a later subscriber (fold) raises, or vice versa, the event is partially applied — in-memory fold state and the persisted event log can diverge, violating 'state reconstructable purely from events' (a replay hazard, R5). The single existing error-isolation test (test_error_isolation) asserts the ExceptionGroup abort as correct rather than exercising subscriber tiering.

confirmed.title: Instant heat-threshold rupture path is unreachable in integrated play; only isolation tests exercise it

confirmed.title: Sensor noise sub-seed is keyed only on (tick, sensor_id), so multiple observations reuse the same draw

A FRESH Random is derived each call from the same (seed, tick, sensor_id) and drawn exactly once, so every target observed by that sensor this tick gets the IDENTICAL noise value; two mechs carrying the same sensor model also share the identical noise. The `for_event` positional named `mech_id` is being fed a sensor_id, so a sensor_id colliding with a mech_id would share sub-seeds.

confirmed.title: Unreachable `except TimeoutError` branch in OpenAICompatibleClient.complete

No code path raises a builtin TimeoutError here.

It is dead code that obscures the real control flow for a maintainer reasoning about timeout classification.

confirmed.title: Overload-regression gate is battery-size-dependent, not a rate
confirmed.evidence: `_compute_overload_rate_delta` (promotion.py:127-138) returns `(candidate_total - parent_total) / n` where `n = len(search_outcomes) + len(holdout_outcomes)` (a count of SEED-OUTCOMES) and each outcome's `candidate_overloads` is itself a SUM of BOILER_OVERLOADED events over that seed's two duels (duel_evaluator.py:109). This is net overload-events-per-seed, not a rate in [0,1], but the threshold field is named `max_overload_rate_increase` (promotion.py:41) with default 0.05 and compared at promotion.py:216.
confirmed.failure_mode: The same candidate behavior (say, 2 extra overload events across the battery) yields delta=2/40=0.05 (passes) with a 20-search+20-holdout battery but 2/20=0.10 (rejected as OVERLOAD_REGRESSION) with a 10+10 battery. Promotion outcomes therefore depend on the operator's chosen `--seeds/--holdout` sizes rather than on a genuine per-match overload rate, making gate verdicts non-comparable across configs and the default 0.05 effectively a near-zero-tolerance knob whose meaning shifts with battery size.
confirmed.recommendation: Normalize to a true rate: divide candidate/parent overload counts by the number of matches (duels) each side actually played, then take the difference of rates; or rename the field and document the per-seed-net semantics and its battery-size dependence. Pin the intended semantics with a test that varies battery size and holds the verdict constant.
confirmed.verify_reason: The mechanical fact holds — _compute_overload_rate_delta (promotion.py:127-138) returns (candidate_total - parent_total)/n over seed-outcome counts where candidate_overloads is a summed BOILER_OVERLOADED count (duel_evaluator.py:109), so it is an unbounded per-seed average net count, not a [0,1] rate, yet is compared to a field named max_overload_rate_increase=0.05 — but the headline 'battery-size-dependent verdict for the same behavior' failure mode is largely wrong: dividing by n is the correct normalization that makes the metric battery-size-stable in expectation (the reviewer's example holds total extra overloads fixed while a genuine per-seed effect scales with n), so this is a naming/semantic imprecision, not a medium logic bug.

confirmed.title: Live-provider grant max_completions is a dead/misleading budget; the real per-completion meter is a separate hardcoded BoundedLlmClient(256)

confirmed.title: Browser gateway ↔ real authority/coordinator seam is tested only against fakes that discard the authority context

Both the unit double (_Start.admit_start_match does `del context`, test_browser_gateway.py:74) and the integration 'loopback' double (Start.admit_start_match does `del context, match_id`, test_browser_gateway_loopback.py:181-190) discard the context entirely. The actual browser→authority seat-authority seam could silently admit a seat the session does not own.

confirmed.title: dispatch_runtime has no gateway-level idempotency/conflict cache; idempotency is delegated to the unconstrained _RuntimePort protocol
confirmed.evidence: start_match and submit_action keep _start_results/_action_results + owner maps and short-circuit duplicates before touching the coordinator (browser_gateway.py:230-233,269-278,336-346). dispatch_runtime has NO such cache: under the lock it calls `self._runtime.dispatch(command)` on every delivery and rebuilds a fresh ModelSOBrowserRuntimeAccepted (browser_gateway.py:378-400). The class/test claim idempotency ('...is_authenticated_and_idempotent', test line 200), but the guarantee holds only because MatchRuntime.dispatch dedupes by command_id (runtime.py:240-246). The injected _RuntimePort protocol only requires `dispatch(...) -> RuntimeCommandReceipt` (browser_gateway.py:196-197) and imposes no dedup contract.

The 'one-shot semantics' the gateway advertises are convention-dependent, not enforced.

confirmed.title: Human turn prompts hardcode a thin action menu (1 of 6 move directions, full speed only), a behavior policy baked into code not a contract
confirmed.evidence: _prompt_actions offers a human exactly one MOVE: `ModelSOMovePlayerAction(kind="move", direction="toward_enemy", speed="full")` (coordinator.py:88) and one disengage `direction="defensive"` (coordinator.py:114-119). area_summaries.summary: The envelope's top-level fields are genuinely closed (extra="forbid", frozen, UUID identities preserved via ModelEnvelope composition), and the per-event-type payload authorities in payloads.py/card_payloads.py are rigorous. But the event boundary itself does NOT enforce those authorities: payload is stored as a raw FrozenJSONMapping with no event_type↔payload cross-check, so "closedness" is a consumer-side convention. That convention is guarded only by a hand-maintained AST allowlist that already omits at least one real raw-payload consumer (llm/adaptation.py, which reads env.payload.get("action","?") with a silent default). Determinism/identity evidence (provenance, hashes, seat identity) is optional in MATCH_STARTED, weakening replay evidence and the seat-differentiation anchor. Several lower-severity issues: dead duplicate caused_by, unvalidated envelope schema_version, and a dead PILOT_INJURED open-payload vocabulary entry.

The domain contract models are individually well-built (closed extra="forbid" boundaries, UUID preservation, canonical hashing, strong seat-provenance on the roster/catalog path). The severe problems are at the seams and in the shipped default demo overlay, not in single models. The marquee split-deck demo (tactical_split_v1_qwen.yaml) binds BOTH seats to the berserker pilot despite labeling blue a "sniper," and nothing in the contract layer reconciles a seat's deck-policy archetype with its programmer's actual persona — so seat identity is a cosmetic label, defeating the finish-line goal of strategically different trajectories. The same overlay opts both seats into failure_policy: fallback, which silently degrades a live-provider failure to a deterministic plan with no durable event marker, contradicting the finish-line rule that fallback be an explicit failure mode. Determinism evidence is also weakened: the card-runtime provenance model cannot represent split decks and emits nothing in split mode.

The DI composition graph is disciplined about closing provider/ledger resources and about fail-closed provider selection, but it does NOT enforce the load-bearing "admitted seat identity is one validated contract" invariant at the boundary where the actual behavioral driver (card programmers) is built. In paced card mode — the default demo mode — the validated decide-pilot identity is inert and the card programmer that actually pilots each seat is never cross-checked against the admitted seat archetype/pilot_spec, so a blue "sniper" seat runs the berserker programmer/persona and no ledger evidence reveals it. Separately, a worker crash leaves the runtime FSM stuck in RUNNING with no terminal status (no FAILED state exists, and non-boundary errors emit no MATCH_ENDED), so a real-provider failure never reaches a durable terminal result. Several behavior-governing constants (completion budget, default failure policy) live in core composition code rather than in a contract field.

The fold/state layer is clean and canonical (single delta() reducer, closed models, contract-injected catalog), but the runner's sudden-death convergence and card-mode seat handling contain real finish-line blockers. Verified at runtime: a symmetric uncapped match ALWAYS hands the win to the alphabetically-later mech (mech.b/blue) with full HP, seed-independent — a deterministic side bias that breaks the side-swap symmetry the learning loop depends on and turns a mutual-destruction into a false win. Separately, the default demo's "berserker vs sniper" seat differentiation is almost entirely cosmetic in the card path (shared decks, shared LLM persona, unused archetype label), and in card mode the injected loadout pilots are required-but-never-invoked while MATCH_STARTED records the wrong (loadout) pilot as the seat's decision-maker. These directly undermine the "strategically DIFFERENT trajectories, durable/legible terminal, replayable evidence" finish line.

The delegated reducers (boiler, failure, lifecycle, movement) are cleanly folded by MatchStateFold and are largely R3/R5-clean (closed payloads, UUID correlation ids, seeded RNG, replay==live by construction). But mode has a fully dead second implementation that diverges from the canonical fold, and two terminal-correctness gaps threaten the finish line: a rupture-induced mutual KO produces no winner/terminal event, and the documented instant heat-rupture path is unreachable in real matches while its unit tests pass on a fabricated surrogate. A robustness gap in pilot_tick lets one malformed pilot decision abort the whole match.

The pure card layer (dealer/reducer/round/rules) is genuinely deterministic, closed-boundary, and wired into the live match via match/card_adapter.py + composition.py — so it is NOT dead. But "declarative combat variety" is largely an illusion: the KNOWN-ANCHOR seat-identity split is real (blue's "sniper" deck-policy archetype runs the berserker LLM persona, and the deck_policy.archetype field is never read by any handler), the only implemented programming rule is inert in every shipped overlay and is even a structural no-op under the shipped deck shape, and every deck sets register_count == hand_size so no side ever SELECTS cards — only reorders them. I also found a concrete match-crashing logic bug: a register that stays heat-locked for two consecutive card rounds hits a fail-closed error because previous_plan is rebuilt from free-registers-only plan_committed. Net: seat/archetype differentiation and rule-driven variety do not survive to the ledger as real behavior; they are cosmetic labels plus RNG.

The provider protocol, HTTP client, evidence-effect decorator, and stub are individually well-built (closed strict models, DI-injected transport/secret/sleeper, fail-closed budgets, sanitized transport errors, no provider-specific forks in core sim code). The finish-line-blocking damage is at the seams: the split-deck qwen "demo" overlay binds BOTH programmers to the berserker pilot spec, so the advertised blue "sniper" silently runs the berserker persona (the confirmed anchor) and no validation catches it — killing "strategically DIFFERENT trajectories." Compounding this, that same overlay sets failure_policy: fallback on both seats and the PLAN_COMMITTED event carries no provenance field, so any provider JSON drift silently produces a deterministic priority-planner match that is indistinguishable from a real LLM match in the authoritative (folded) evidence. The declared effect node contract also references a handler class that does not exist and is never dispatched.

The offline learning loop (search -> evaluate -> stats -> gate -> lineage YAML) is well-built, pure, and deterministic. But the "live learning loop" that the finish line requires (P3: promotion as an EVENT, live policy adaptation actually wired) does not exist as a running path. `LiveLearningCoordinator` is dead code: never instantiated in production, no concrete `LiveLearningEvaluator` implementation exists, `begin_match` is never called, and the only hook that could drive it (`AfterMatchLearningHandler`) is wired with `promotion=None`. Where promotion happens at all, it is an in-memory `current_policy` mutation or a YAML file on disk — never an event in the ledger, and there is no promotion event type in `SOEventType`. Two blockers plus a seam mismatch and a green-on-surrogate test mean live policy adaptation is evidence-only, not wired.

The commands-gateway is unusually disciplined: fail-closed authentication, closed extra="forbid"/strict models, UUID-preserving correlation, thread-safe process-lifetime idempotency, and (on the live browser path) the launch provenance carrying per-seat identity does reach the MATCH_STARTED ledger payload — so the anchor's "cosmetic seat label" fear is NOT realized here as long as the roster differs per side. No fail-open blocker was found. The residual defects are contract-drift and coverage gaps: a live-provider "budget" field that nothing meters, the gateway↔real-coordinator authority seam tested only against fakes that discard context, runtime-command idempotency that works only by convention, a hidden hardcoded human action-menu policy, and no guard against a boring mirror-persona default match.

The SQLite ledger is genuinely strict and append-only (DB triggers + Pydantic round-trip codec), and the replay engine has real, tested provenance gates for card-runtime and card-rule-pack drift. But the replay layer has a load-bearing gap directly on the finish-line anchor: seat/launch identity (pilot_spec_id / persona_id / loadout_id / model_identity_id per side) is round-tripped as opaque bytes and is NEVER validated by the replay engine, while card provenance IS — so the qwen35-vs-qwen35_sniper seat mismatch is invisible to replay-verified truth. The single replay-equality gate (verify_replay_validity) compares only ModelSOMatchState, which excludes provider/persona/model-output identity, so it proves physics reconstruction, not provider fidelity. There is one storage impl (SQLite) — no Postgres second path exists, so the "one protocol" rule is not violated — but ledger-open re-validates every row of every match against current models with no isolation, so a single schema-drifted row denies read access to all matches.

The CLI/projection surfaces are individually well-tested, but two finish-line blockers hide in the composition seams that live in this area. (1) Seat-identity differentiation only survives on the `--catalog-index` path: the named default demo overlay `tactical_split_v1_qwen` binds BOTH card programmers to `pilot.llm.qwen35` (berserker persona), and nothing rebinds the roster/browser seat selection into the card programmer on the direct-overlay path — so a blue "sniper" seat is silently programmed by the berserker persona, yielding samey trajectories. (2) The default demo overlay sets `failure_policy: fallback` on both seats, and the fallback emits an unlabeled deterministic plan, so a provider outage silently masquerades as a real LLM match — exactly the failure mode the finish line forbids. The REST "replayable evidence" endpoint is defined+tested but never mounted, and the anchor defect is not covered by any test.

The pilot schemas, heuristic pilots, immutable adapters, and in-process bus are individually well-modeled (extra="forbid" everywhere, deterministic heuristics, golden parity harnesses). The load-bearing defect is the confirmed anchor: seat identity does NOT survive into the LLM programming path — ModelSOProgrammingObservation carries a bare seat string with no archetype/persona/pilot identity, and program_for_seat validates only that string, so a blue "sniper" and red "berserker" both bound to pilot.llm.qwen35 run the identical persona. The other real issues are a decision model whose action_params is an open JSON bag validated only after the authoritative PILOT_DECISION_MADE event is already committed, and a bus that re-raises every subscriber failure (including best-effort UI/transport subscribers) with no atomicity, coupling a browser/WS failure to abort of the authoritative sim.

The default demo overlay tactical_split_v1_qwen is broken at the seat-identity level: its split-deck policy labels the blue seat "sniper" but binds BOTH programmers to pilot.llm.qwen35 (persona=berserker), so the blue "sniper" silently flies the berserker prompt — the exact anchor bug. This is not isolated: every qwen/glm overlay binds both seats to one persona while shipping an unused differentiated partner spec in the same registry dir; only the gemini/openrouter overlays actually differentiate. No validator cross-checks programmer-persona against seat archetype (the seat archetype label is in fact dead data), and the test suite is green precisely because it asserts the samey binding as correct. The correctly-differentiated roster contract (canonical_qwen35) exists and is validated, but the demo runs the parallel, un-validated programmers path instead — a second semantic seat-selection path that disagrees with it.

The parser layer (types.ts) is genuinely strong: closed payloads, unknown-field rejection, cross-field invariants, and a real Python-fixture parity harness. But the layer above it drops load-bearing contract data on the floor: the authoritative per-seat identity contract (launch_provenance.seat_assignments) and the split-deck programming plan (plan_committed) are strictly parsed yet rendered nowhere, so the exact thing the known anchor demands — provable seat differentiation reaching the browser — is invisible. The transport's terminal guard also hard-crashes on the draw scoring path, and the one "real match" regression test replays a legacy side-less heuristic ledger, leaving the entire finish-line demo path (real providers, split decks, red/blue trajectories, scorecard) with no end-to-end coverage. A dead view cluster ships alongside a test that certifies an unmounted component.

Steel Onslaught has a genuinely strong shipped substrate (event-sourced reducer, split-deck card system, an ambitious Pressure Deck UI, asymmetric qwen loadouts), but the finish-line "wow" — two LLMs producing visibly DIFFERENT, legible, shareable trajectories — does not actually survive to the default demo path. The confirmed anchor is worse than a label bug: in card mode the overlay's card programmers (both bound to the berserker pilot) are what decide, so the blue "sniper" seat is piloted by a berserker "rush to point-blank" brain that contradicts its own recorded seat identity, and nothing validates the two. Compounding this, the demo runs card/paced mode where NO pilot_decision_made events exist, so the designed "watch the LLM think" decision-row centerpiece never renders, the tactical-variety handlers are left unwired (handler_ids: []), and both seats draw from identical decks. The net effect is two same-doctrine mechs whose reasoning is invisible — the opposite of the shareable moment the design promises.
